papers.full_text: Proteases from Bacillus licheniformis destroy Aedes aegypti larvae Ana Carolina Silva Universidade Federal de Lavras Ruth Celestina Condori Mamani Universidade Federal de Lavras Amanda do Carmo Alves Universidade Federal de Lavras Jhennifer Cristiana Souza Universidade Federal de Lavras Ludimila Vieira Fernandes Universidade Federal de Lavras Ingrid Marciano Alvarenga Universidade Federal de Lavras Joziana Muniz Paiva Barçante Universidade Federal de Lavras Pedro Henryque Castro Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais Grasielle D ́ Avila Pessoa Caldas Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais Filippe Elias Freitas Soares Universidade Federal de Lavras Short Report Keywords: Aedes aegypti, protease, biochemical control, larvicidal, toxicity Posted Date: September 23rd, 2026 DOI: https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-10120306/v1 License:   This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License. Read Full License Page 1/12 Additional Declarations: No competing interests reported. Page 2/12 Abstract Controlling the Aedes aegypti vector, which transmits arboviruses such as DENV (dengue), ZIKV (Zika), and CHIKV (chikungunya), represents a global challenge that requires the development of new biotechnological larvicides. This study evaluated the efficacy of a formulation containing proteases derived from Bacillus licheniformis at different concentrations (0.1%, 0.5%, 1.0%, and 1.5% w/v) on early third-instar larvae. Toxicity bioassays revealed a dose- and time-dependent larvicidal effect. In the first 24 hours, the highest concentration (1.5%) achieved 80% mortality, rising to 100% after 72 hours. In contrast, the control and denatured formulation groups remained viable, demonstrating that lethality is dependent on the enzymatic activity of the proteases (p < 0.05). Morphological analysis by light microscopy corroborated the quantitative data, revealing cuticular disintegration and leakage of visceral contents in larvae exposed to the highest doses, evidencing the tissue damage caused by the formulation. The results indicate that the protease derived from B. licheniformis tested has high potential as a fast-acting larvicide, presenting itself as an alternative for integrated vector management strategies. Introduction Aedes aegypti is a mosquito of enormous public health importance, as it serves as the primary vector for arboviruses such as DENV, ZIKV, and CHIKV, which affect millions of people annually, especially in tropical and subtropical regions. The wide geographic distribution of this insect, combined with its high adaptive capacity and ability to thrive in urban environments, contributes to the recurring increase in epidemic outbreaks and to the difficulty in controlling the vector population. Thus, effective and sustainable strategies for reducing larval populations are essential to minimize the transmission of these arboviruses (Serdeiro et al., 2023, Vasantha-Srinivasan et al.,2024). Chemical control, based primarily on the use of synthetic larvicides, has been widely employed as a method to combat the mosquito. However, the use of chemical agents can cause environmental impacts, toxicity to non-target organisms, and, most importantly, the development of resistance by natural insect populations (Zulfa et al., 2022). Given these limitations, there is growing interest in biotechnological and biological alternatives that offer greater selectivity and lower ecological risk, as they are considered more suitable for integrated vector control programs (Sengul Demirak and Canpolat, 2022). Among the alternative methods for controlling A. aegypti, metabolites produced by microorganisms— particularly bacteria of the genus Bacillus—stand out for their ability to synthesize bioactive compounds and hydrolytic enzymes with insecticidal potential (Falqueto et al., 2021). In this context, formulations based on Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis (Bti) have been widely used for larval control, acting through crystalline toxins (Cry, Cyt1Aa) that promote the lysis of intestinal epithelial cells after ingestion (Brühl et al.,2020; Menezes et al.,2025). Although Bti-based formulations are widely used in the biological control of A. aegypti due to their high efficacy, the development of cell-free biotechnology products has broadened the prospects for larval Page 3/12 control. The application of Bti-based products relies on the use of spores and protein crystals, whose stability and performance can be influenced by environmental and operational factors (Brühl et al., 2020). In contrast, enzymatic formulations composed of purified biomolecules do not require the release of viable microorganisms into the environment, which can simplify aspects related to production, formulation, and application. Furthermore, the mechanism of action of Bti is associated with the ingestion and activation of toxins in the larvae’s gut (Brühl et al., 2020; Menezes et al., 2025), whereas exogenous bacterial proteases have the potential to act on different biological structures, including the cuticle and the peritrophic matrix (Nimbulkar et al., 2025). This characteristic suggests a multi-target action, capable of compromising the insect’s physical and physiological barriers, as well as enhancing the penetration and efficacy of other biological control agents when used in combined strategies. In this scenario, the present study evaluated the larvicidal efficacy of a commercial formulation of B. licheniformis proteases, at different concentrations, against third-instar (L3) larvae of A. aegypti. Larval mortality was evaluated over a period of 72 h. Additionally, the stability of the formulation’s proteolytic activity was investigated under conditions similar to those of the bioassay. Materials and Methods Obtaining and maintaining Aedes aegypti Aedes aegypti (Rockefeller strain) were obtained from the colony maintained at the Parasitic Biology Laboratory II (Department of Medicine, Federal University of Lavras). The females were fed with hamsters, in accordance with the protocol approved by the Animal Ethics Committee (CEUA) of the UFLA Office of the Vice-Rector for Research (No. 026/21). The eggs were incubated in 1.5 L of dechlorinated tap water in rectangular plastic containers with lids (40 × 12 × 12 cm). The larvae were fed crushed fish feed and maintained at 25 ± 2°C under a 12:12 h photoperiod (light:dark). After five days, third-stage (L3) larvae were obtained and used in the bioassays. Obtaining the enzyme The commercial formulation of B. licheniformis proteases (HPF) was kindly provided by Prozyn® (São Paulo, Brazil). Stability of the enzyme formulation Proteolytic activity was measured using the caseinolytic assay (Braga et al., 2011). For this assay, a solution containing 0.5 mL of 1% (w/v) casein, 0.45 mL of 100 mM Tris-HCl buffer, pH 8, and 0.05 mL of the enzymatic formulation at 0.1% or 1.5% (w/v) were incubated at 50°C for 15 min in test tubes. After this time, the reaction was stopped by adding 1 mL of 10% (w/v) trichloroacetic acid (TCA). Immediately thereafter, the solutions were centrifuged at 10,000 g for 10 min. The supernatant was recovered for Page 4/12 measurement in a UV-Vis spectrophotometer at 280 nm. One enzyme unit was defined as the amount of protease required to release 1 μg of tyrosine per minute under test conditions. To evaluate the stability of the B. licheniformis protease formulation, proteolytic activity was measured at 24, 48 and 72 hours. A solution of the proteolytic product was prepared using dechlorinated tap water and subsequently incubated at 27 ± 1°C under the same conditions as the bioassay with the larvae. In vitro assay on Aedes aegypti larvae (L) A bioassay to evaluate the effect of B. licheniformis proteases on third-instar larvae of A. aegypti was conducted according to World Health Organization guidelines, with modifications. Six experimental groups were established: a control group containing only dechlorinated water (G1); a control group containing the denatured formulation (boiled for 2 hours) (G2); and four treatment groups: HPF (G3) (1.5% w/v), HPF (G4) (1% w/v), HPF (G5) (0.5% w/v), and HPF (G6) (0.1% w/v). For each experimental group, 50 mL of solution prepared in dechlorinated water and 30 third-instar (L3) larvae of A. aegypti were used. The assay was conducted in plastic cups (4.5 cm in diameter × 8.5 cm in height), with five replicates for each group, and was repeated three times on different days. Mortality was assessed over three days. Larvae were considered dead when they could not reach the surface of the solution upon shaking the cups, and also when they showed no signs of movement, even after being gently touched with a glass rod. If pupae formed, they were considered live larvae. All groups were incubated at 27 ± 1°C, and the larvae were fed daily (Falvo et al., 2018). Statistical Analysis The bioassay data were initially subjected to the Shapiro-Wilk and Bartlett tests to assess normality and homoscedasticity. Following this assessment, a one-way ANOVA was performed using BioEstat software version 5.3 to evaluate differences between treatment groups. When ANOVA indicated significant differences, Tukey’s test was applied for paired comparisons of means. The confidence interval was 99% (Ayres et al., 2003). The mean percentage of larval mortality (L3) was calculated using the equation below, described by Mendoza-De-Gives and Vazquez-Prats (Mendoza-De Gives and Vazquez-Prats, 1994). %Reduction = (Average of control − Average of treatment) × 100 Average of control Results Stability of the enzyme formulation Page 5/12 The stability of the B. licheniformis proteases was evaluated at the highest and lowest concentrations used in the bioassay (0.1% and 1.5%). The results are presented in Table 1. Table 1 Assessment of the stability of proteolytic activity (U/mL) in the protease formulation derived from Bacillus licheniformis (HPF), supplied by Prozyn®, under the same conditions as those used in the in vitro assay on Aedes aegypti larvae. Proteolytic activity (± U/mL) HPF concentration 24h 48h 72h 0.1% (w/v) 154.44(± 0.003) 150.16(± 0.004) 151.03(± 0.002) 1.5% (w/v) 204.88(± 0.011) 200.44(± 0.021) 189.51(± 0.018) In vitro assay on Aedes aegypti larvae (L) According to the results, dose-dependent and time-dependent larvicidal activity was observed (Fig. 1). The negative control group and the group containing the denatured formulation showed no mortality, maintaining 100% larval viability throughout the experiment, with no statistically significant difference between them (p > 0.05). In the first 24 hours, the highest concentration (1.5% (w/v)) caused 83.3% mortality, differing significantly from the control (p < 0.01), while the lowest concentration (0.1% (w/v)) resulted in 53.3% mortality. After 72 hours of exposure to the treatments, the efficacy of the 1.5% (w/v) formulation reached 100% mortality, while the 0.1% (w/v) concentration resulted in 83.3% larval mortality. Intra-period statistical analysis showed that, after 24 hours, the 1.0% and 1.5% (w/v) concentrations exhibited greater toxicity than the lower doses (p < 0.01). At the 48-hour and 72-hour time points, the mortality rate increased in all treated groups, with the 1.5% (w/v) dose being significantly more effective than the others (p < 0.05), except for the similarity observed among the higher doses in the final stages of the experiment (p > 0.05). Figure 2 illustrates the morphological changes caused by exposure to protease. It is noted that, at a concentration of 1.5% (w/v) (Fig. 2D), there is an extravasation of the visceral contents, evidencing the proteolytic effect of the formulation. Discussion The enzymatic formulation containing protease derived from B. licheniformis exhibited significant larvicidal activity against A. aegypti larvae (L3), with a dose-dependent pattern and an increasing mortality rate over time. The 83% mortality of larvae within the first 24 h at a concentration of 1.5% (w/v) and complete mortality within 72 h indicate that the enzyme acts rapidly and efficiently to compromise Page 6/12 larval survival. t is important to highlight that even the lowest concentration tested (0.1% w/v; 1 mg/mL) caused approximately 95% mortality after 72 hours. It indicates substantial biological activity at a concentration 15 times lower than that required to achieve complete mortality. This finding is relevant from an application standpoint, since high efficacy at low concentrations can reduce the demand for protease and improve the economic viability of large-scale production and field implementation. Furthermore, these results corroborate findings in the literature demonstrating that bacterial enzymes, especially chitinases and proteases, act on essential insect structures, such as the cuticle and the midgut epithelium, promoting the degradation of structural and digestive components, which leads to tissue lysis, physiological disorganization, and, consequently, the death of the organism (Mahathir et al., 2025 and Pineda and Castellanos-Rozo, 2025). Possible mechanisms of action of bacterial proteases on A. aegypti larvae are mainly associated with the degradation of the peritrophic matrix, a layer composed of chitin and glycoproteins that protects the intestinal epithelium of the insect or larva (Vasantha-Srinivasam et al., 2024). Proteolytic activity promotes the breakdown of this barrier, increasing permeability and exposing epithelial cells to direct damage. Additionally, these enzymes may interfere with the activity of digestive proteases such as trypsin and chymotrypsin, impairing digestion and nutrient absorption. As a result, there is disruption of the intestinal epithelium, nutritional deficiency, and physiological collapse, leading to the death of the larvae (Shamsi et al., 2018). The proteolytic activity observed in this study is consistent with the study by Katak et al., (2021), who used supernatants from different strains of Bacillus ssp. containing hydrolytic enzymes. These supernatants were lyophilized and dissolved in distilled water to a concentration of 5 mg/mL. This solution resulted in a 93% mortality rate among A. aegypti larvae after 72 hours of exposure. However, an important advantage of the present study is the use of a commercial enzymatic product (HPF) from B. licheniformis, which allows larval mortality to be attributed directly to proteolytic activity, eliminating the variability and combined effects of multiple metabolites present in bacterial supernatants (Fig. 2). It is important to note that the bioassays in this study were conducted using third-instar (L3) A. aegypti larvae, a stage in which individuals exhibit greater physiological robustness, a thicker cuticle, and more developed defense mechanisms compared to earlier stages (Farnesi et al., 2012). For this reason, the high mortality rates observed in L3 suggest that proteases are highly effective in later instars. In other words, it is expected that A. aegypti larvae in earlier instars (L1 and L2), which have thinner cuticles and lower detoxification capacity, will be even more susceptible to enzymatic action, possibly resulting in even faster and more pronounced mortality. A comparison with studies involving other bacteria that produce larvicidal enzymes, such as Pseudomonas putida and various species of Bacillus and Serratia, shows that the use of hydrolases such as proteases causes damage to the cuticle and digestive system, resulting in high mortality within the first 48–72 hours (Jupatanakul et al., 2020 and Mini and Mathew, 2023). Therefore, the results reinforce Page 7/12 that the proteases of B. licheniformis possess characteristics consistent with the efficacy patterns already reported for other bacterial species applied as biocontrol agents. The formulation used in this study maintained enzymatic activity for 72 h under the same conditions as the bioassay with the larvae. A relevant point to consider, given that enzymes tend to experience a reduction in enzymatic activity due to variations in temperature, pH, and contact with other organic and inorganic compounds (Nelson and Cox, 2017), is that the water used for the assay was dechlorinated tap water; that is, other elements were present in it, such as fluoride and calcium, among others. These data indicate the potential for practical use of these proteases, especially in domestic or peri-urban applications, where sustained activity is necessary to target heterogeneous larval populations over time. Finally, the results obtained demonstrate that the B. licheniformis protease is a promising alternative for the development of bioinsecticide formulations intended for the control of A. aegypti. In addition to exhibiting high stability in tap water throughout the experimental period, the enzyme evaluated achieved mortality rates of approximately 95% at a concentration of just 0.1% (w/v) after 72 hours of exposure, demonstrating its potential for effectiveness even at low concentrations. These characteristics, combined with the growing demand for more sustainable and environmentally safe control strategies, reinforce the potential of this technology for applications in vector management. However, before its large-scale implementation, additional studies are needed to evaluate its persistence under real-world field conditions, its interaction with organic matter and other environmental components, and possible synergistic effects with biological agents already used in mosquito control, as well as its stability and enzymatic activity under different environmental conditions. papers.title_zh: 利福尼亚芽孢杆菌蛋白酶破坏埃及伊蚊幼虫
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Controlling the Aedes aegypti vector, which transmits arboviruses such as DENV (dengue), ZIKV (Zika), and CHIKV (chikungunya), represents a global challenge that requires the development of new biotechnological larvicides. This study evaluated the efficacy of a formulation containing proteases derived from Bacillus licheniformis at different concentrations (0.1%, 0.5%, 1.0%, and 1.5% w/v) on early third-instar larvae. Toxicity bioassays revealed a dose- and time-dependent larvicidal effect. In the first 24 hours, the highest concentration (1.5%) achieved 80% mortality, rising to 100% after 72 hours. In contrast, the control and denatured formulation groups remained viable, demonstrating that lethality is dependent on the enzymatic activity of the proteases (p B. licheniformis tested has high potential as a fast-acting larvicide, presenting itself as an alternative for integrated vector management strategies.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 控制传播登革热病毒(DENV)、寨卡病毒(ZIKV)和基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)等虫媒病毒的埃及伊蚊(Aedes aegypti)媒介是一项全球性挑战,需要开发新的生物技术杀幼虫剂。本研究评估了含有从利福尼亚芽孢杆菌(Bacillus licheniformis)提取的蛋白酶制剂在不同浓度(0.1%、0.5%、1.0%和1.5% w/v)下对早期第三龄幼虫的效果。毒性生物测定显示杀幼虫效果具有剂量和时间依赖性。在前24小时内,最高浓度(1.5%)达到80% 死亡率,72小时后升至100%。相比之下,对照组和变性制剂组的幼虫仍然存活,这表明致死性依赖于蛋白酶的酶活性(p < 0.05)。利福尼亚芽孢杆菌测试的蛋白酶具有作为快速作用杀幼虫剂的高潜力,为综合媒介管理策略提供了替代方案。

papers.title: [Fever in returning travelers : what's new in 2026 ?].
papers.abstract: Fever upon returning from a travel to tropical areas poses a diagnostic challenge due to the multitude of possible causes. Although most cases are related to common or benign infections, it is imperative to rapidly rule out potentially severe conditions, mostly malaria and dengue. Recent developments include the geographic spread of arboviral diseases and the introduction of vaccines for dengue fever and chikungunya.

papers.title: Backs under pressure: measuring and estimating lumbar spinal loads.
papers.abstract: This issue of the Biomedical Journal examines lumbar spinal loading and current approaches to its assessment using invasive measurements, biomechanical modeling, imaging, wearable technologies, and AI-assisted methods. Other contributions address coumarin derivatives as modulators of autophagy and PI3K/mTOR signaling in cancer and apply multi-omics approaches to uric acid metabolism and cardiometabolic disease. Further studies investigate molecular mechanisms linking mechanical irritation to oral squamous cell carcinoma progression, predictors of HBsAg seroclearance after antiviral treatment withdrawal, and age-dependent effects of exercise and losartan. Additional contributions explore PD-L1 signaling in allergic asthma, the antiviral activity of BPR2-D2 against chikungunya virus replication, and differences in objective tear function between patients with and without mental disorders.

analysis.methods: The editorial discussed various approaches to lumbar spinal load assessment, including invasive measurements, biomechanical modeling, imaging, wearable technologies, and AI-assisted methods, but did not detail specific experimental procedures.
analysis.main_results: The editorial highlighted the diversity of methods used to measure lumbar spinal loads and noted the need for further studies to explore molecular mechanisms and predictors related to health outcomes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as emphasizing the importance of integrating multiple techniques for accurate assessment of spinal loads and identified gaps in understanding the biological and clinical implications of these measurements.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that improved methods for measuring spinal loads could enhance the understanding of musculoskeletal conditions and inform better prevention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to an editorial review, which does not provide empirical data, and therefore the confidence in the findings is low.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为强调整合多种技术以准确评估脊柱载荷的重要性,并指出了对这些测量的生物学和临床意义理解上的不足。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,改进的脊柱载荷测量方法可以增强对肌肉骨骼疾病的理解,并为更好的预防策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于编辑综述,未提供实证数据,因此对研究结果的信心较低。

papers.abstract_zh: 本期《生物医学杂志》探讨了腰椎脊柱载荷及其当前评估方法,包括侵入性测量、生物力学建模、影像学、可穿戴技术以及人工智能辅助方法。其他贡献涉及香豆素衍生物作为癌症中自噬和PI3K/mTOR信号通路调节剂的研究,以及利用多组学方法研究尿酸代谢和心血管代谢性疾病。进一步的研究探讨了机械刺激与口腔鳞状细胞癌进展之间的分子机制,HBsAg血清清除率的预测因素,以及运动和洛沙坦的年龄依赖性效应。其他贡献还涉及PD-L1信号在过敏性哮喘中的作用,BPR2-D2对基孔肯雅病毒复制的抗病毒药物活性,以及患有和未患有精神障碍患者之间客观泪液功能的差异。

papers.title: Clinical Mimickers of Mpox: A Case Series from a Tropical Referral Center
papers.abstract: Mpox is a zoonotic disease caused by the monkeypox virus, a double-stranded DNA virus belonging to the genus Orthopoxvirus. The World Health Organization (WHO) declared mpox a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) in July 2022 amid the global clade IIb outbreak and again in August 2024 following an increase in cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo associated with clades Ia and Ib. Despite increased awareness, diagnosing mpox remains challenging because its clinical manifestations often overlap with those of other infectious and non-infectious conditions. This diagnostic challenge occurs across geographic settings but may be further complicated in tropical regions by the circulation of locally prevalent infections, including arboviral diseases such as dengue and chikungunya. Here, we describe a series of nine patients initially evaluated for suspected mpox, in whom alternative diagnoses were subsequently established.

papers.title: Solanaceae-Derived Spirostane Saponins Inhibit Dengue Virus Replication and Viral Protein Expression and Exhibit Activity Against Multiple Arboviruses.
papers.abstract: Mosquito-borne arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), represent a growing global health burden, yet no specific antiviral therapies are currently available for most of these infections. This unmet need highlights the importance of identifying novel antiviral compounds from biologically relevant sources such as plant-derived natural products. In this study, a bioactivity-guided approach was applied to methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species to identify compounds with antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells. Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Subsequent fractionation and purification led to the isolation of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, structurally characterized by UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy. Functional assays demonstrated that these compounds inhibit DENV replication, as evidenced by marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers. Stage-specific analyses revealed that their antiviral activity is primarily associated with intracellular phases of the viral life cycle, consistent with inhibition of viral replication and/or protein processing. Molecular docking analyses supported these findings by predicting favorable interactions with key viral enzymes, particularly NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and NS3 helicase/protease. Importantly, the isolated compounds retained antiviral activity against ZIKV and CHIKV, indicating cross-arboviral efficacy. Together, these findings identify spirostane saponins as promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the antiviral potential of Solanaceae-derived spirostane saponins against dengue virus and other arboviruses. The research highlights the need for novel antiviral therapies against mosquito-borne viruses, which currently lack specific treatments. Using a bioactivity-guided approach, the study identifies compounds that significantly reduce viral infectivity and replication in Vero cells. The results indicate that these saponins may have broad-spectrum antiviral activity, as they retain efficacy against related viruses such as chikungunya virus. The findings suggest that spirostane saponins could serve as promising antiviral scaffolds for further development. However, the study is limited to in vitro experiments, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of in vivo or clinical validation.

papers.abstract_zh: 由蚊子传播的虫媒病毒,包括登革病毒(DENV)、寨卡病毒(ZIKV)和基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV),构成了日益增长的全球健康负担,但目前针对这些感染的特定抗病毒药物疗法尚不普及。这种未满足的需求凸显了从生物相关来源(如植物来源的天然产物)中识别新型抗病毒药物化合物的重要性。本研究采用生物活性引导的方法,对八种茄科植物的甲醇提取物进行筛选,以鉴定具有抗病毒药物活性的化合物,针对Vero细胞中的DENV-2。五种提取物显著降低了病毒感染性,其中Solanum ovalifolium和Cestrum sp.在非细胞毒性浓度下实现了完全抑制。随后的分级和纯化过程分离出四种螺甾烷型甾体皂苷,其结构通过UPLC-DAD-MS和1D/2D NMR光谱法进行了表征。功能实验表明,这些化合物抑制了DENV的复制,表现为病毒RNA水平的显著降低、NS1和NS3蛋白表达的减少以及传染性病毒滴度的下降。阶段特异性分析显示,其抗病毒药物活性主要与病毒生命周期的细胞内阶段相关,这与抑制病毒复制和/或蛋白加工一致。分子对接分析支持了这些发现,预测了这些化合物与关键病毒酶的有利相互作用,特别是NS5 RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶和NS3解旋酶/蛋白酶。重要的是,分离出的化合物对ZIKV和CHIKV也表现出抗病毒药物活性,表明其对多种虫媒病毒具有交叉疗效。综上所述,这些发现将螺甾烷皂苷识别为有前景的抗病毒药物骨架,并支持其进一步开发为广谱抗病毒药物药物。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过探索植物来源的新化合物,解决针对蚊媒虫媒病毒(包括基孔肯雅病毒)缺乏特异性抗病毒药物的问题。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用生物活性导向的方法,筛选八种茄科植物的甲醇提取物对DENV-2在Vero细胞中的抗病毒药物活性,并进行后续的分级和纯化以分离活性化合物。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究采用生物活性导向筛选、分级和纯化技术,结合超高效液相色谱-二极管阵列检测-质谱(UPLC-DAD-MS)和一维/二维核磁共振波谱(1D/2D NMR)进行结构表征,并通过功能实验评估抗病毒药物的效果。
analysis_zh.main_results: 五种提取物显著降低了病毒的感染力,其中Solanum ovalifolium和Cestrum sp.在无细胞毒性浓度下实现了完全抑制。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,茄科植物中的螺甾烷皂苷具有针对DENV-2的强效抗病毒药物活性,可能具有广泛的抗病毒药物应用潜力。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为开发针对基孔肯雅病毒及其他相关虫媒病毒的新抗病毒药物提供了基础,为应对新兴病毒感染性疾病提供了潜在的治疗选择。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于体外实验,由于缺乏体内或临床数据,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Factores socioambientales asociados a la persistencia del dengue y otras enfermedades transmitidas por vectores en comunidades de alta prevalencia de la zona sur de Manabí
papers.abstract: Las enfermedades transmitidas por vectores se encuentran entre las principales preocupaciones de salud pública en todo el mundo y equivalen al 17% de los trastornos infecciosos. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar los factores socioambientales asociados a la persistencia del dengue y otras enfermedades transmitidas por vectores en comunidades de alta prevalencia a través de un análisis sistemático de la literatura actual con base en la metodología PRISMA 2020, implicando estudios primarios publicados en bases de datos reconocidas como MEDLINE/PubMed, ScienceDirect, Cochrane Library y Google Scholar entre 2021 a 2026. Los resultados mostraron que la región latinoamericana presenta las mayores prevalencias del virus del dengue, chikungunya, zika y malaria, siendo Colombia y Ecuador los países más afectados. Las temperaturas altas, residir en zonas montosas, rurales, el cambio climático repentino y las lluvias torrenciales son los factores socioambientales más frecuentes. Por último, el estudio entomólogo de vectores, la educación comunitaria, el desarrollo tratamientos y la fumigación recurrente son las medidas de prevención efectivas contra estas patologías. Se concluye que las enfermedades transmitidas tienen un impacto radical en países en desarrollo y solo el trabajo en equipo de instituciones sanitarias y educativas podrían reducir su impacto.
authors: Lady Arianna Parraga de la Cruz

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the socioenvironmental factors associated with the persistence of dengue and other vector-borne diseases in high-prevalence communities in the southern region of Manabí, Ecuador. It highlights the importance of climate variables, such as high temperatures and sudden weather changes, in disease transmission. The research emphasizes the need for integrated prevention strategies, including vector control, community education, treatment development, and recurrent fogging. While the findings suggest that these measures are effective, the study's reliance on a systematic literature review limits its ability to establish direct causality. The results provide valuable insights for public health planning and surveillance in vector-borne disease-endemic areas, particularly in developing countries.

papers.title: PROSPECÇÃO TECNOLÓGICA:UM ESTUDO SOBRE OS DEPÓSITOS DE PATENTES DE NANOEMULSÕES FRENTE AEDES AEGYPTI
papers.abstract: O Aedes aegypti é o vetor das principais arboviroses como a dengue, febre amarela, Zika e Chikungunya. Existem diversas estratégias de controle baseadas na contenção do mosquito, no entanto, mostram-se ineficazes, como a resistência do próprio vetor aos inseticidas químicos. Nesse contexto, novas abordagens biotecnológicas vêm sendo estudadas visando o controle do Ae. Sendo assim, o objetivo desta prospecção tecnológica é analisar, por meio do depósito de patentes o desenvolvimento de inovações relacionadas a nanoemulsões frente o Ae. Foram realizadas buscas de patentes nas bases de dados nacionais e internacionais, como o INPI- Instituto Nacional da Propriedade Industrial e EPO- European Patent Office, entre 2015 a 2025, totalizando 12 patentes analisadas. Verificou-se que o Brasil foi o maior depositante, com 9 patentes. As Universidades apresentaram maior percentual como investidores, com 50%. O Código Internacional de Patentes (CIP) da subclasse A01N e o código A61K, foram os mais frequentes. Por fim, com base nesses resultados, observa-se que ainda há um número reduzido de investimentos em patentes destinadas a inovação de nanoemulsões larvicidas, o que demonstra a importância deste estudo para a percepção e incentivo de mais investimentos em inovação tecnológica desta natureza, no Brasil e no mundo.
papers.journal: Veredas do Direito Direito Ambiental e Desenvolvimento Sustentável

analysis.research_question_and_background: O estudo busca compreender a necessidade de novas estratégias para o controle do Aedes aegypti, que é o vetor das principais arboviroses como a dengue, febre amarela, Zika e Chikungunya. A ineficácia das estratégias atuais, como a resistência do vetor aos inseticidas químicos, justifica a busca por inovações biotecnológicas.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospecção tecnológica analisou patentes depositadas entre 2015 e 2025 nas bases de dados INPI e EPO, com foco em inovações relacionadas a nanoemulsões larvicidas. Foram analisadas 12 patentes, sendo o Brasil o maior depositante com 9 patentes.
analysis.methods: Foram realizadas buscas de patentes nas bases de dados nacionais e internacionais, como o INPI e EPO, entre 2015 e 2025. As patentes foram analisadas com base nos códigos de classificação internacional, como o CIP da subclasse A01N e A61K, e na identificação dos investidores, incluindo universidades.
analysis.main_results: Verificou-se que o Brasil foi o maior depositante de patentes, com 9 patentes, e que as universidades representaram 50% dos investidores. Os códigos CIP da subclasse A01N e A61K foram os mais frequentes entre as patentes analisadas.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Os resultados demonstram que há um número reduzido de investimentos em patentes destinadas a inovações de nanoemulsões larvicidas, o que destaca a relevância do estudo para identificar lacunas e promover novos investimentos em tecnologias biotecnológicas.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: A análise das patentes pode contribuir para a identificação de oportunidades de inovação no controle do Aedes aegypti, especialmente no contexto de doenças como a Chikungunya, que dependem da eficácia de novas estratégias de combate ao vetor.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: A pesquisa baseia-se apenas em dados de patentes, o que limita a profundidade da análise sobre a eficácia ou impacto das inovações. A evidência é considerada moderada, pois depende de registros de depósito, não de estudos experimentais ou clínicos.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a technological prospecting analysis of patents related to nanoemulsions targeting Aedes aegypti, a key vector for arboviruses such as Chikungunya. The research highlights the limited number of patents focused on nanoemulsions for larval control, emphasizing the need for increased investment in this area. The study analyzed 12 patents deposited between 2015 and 2025, with Brazil being the largest contributor. Universities represented 50% of the investors, and the most frequent patent classifications were A01N and A61K. The findings suggest that while there is potential for biotechnological innovation, the current evidence is limited to patent records and does not include experimental or clinical data. The study's implications are primarily for understanding the landscape of technological development in vector control, with moderate confidence in the evidence provided.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,针对杀灭埃及伊蚊的纳米乳剂专利投资仍较为有限,这凸显了本研究的重要性,有助于识别研究空白并推动生物技术领域的创新投资。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 分析专利有助于识别针对埃及伊蚊控制的新创新机会,特别是在基孔肯雅热等依赖有效媒介控制策略的疾病背景下。

papers.title_zh: 技术展望:关于针对埃及伊蚊的纳米乳剂专利池的研究
papers.source_body_en: O Aedes aegypti é o vetor das principais arboviroses como a dengue, febre amarela, Zika e Chikungunya. Existem diversas estratégias de controle baseadas na contenção do mosquito, no entanto, mostram-se ineficazes, como a resistência do próprio vetor aos inseticidas químicos. Nesse contexto, novas abordagens biotecnológicas vêm sendo estudadas visando o controle do Ae. Sendo assim, o objetivo desta prospecção tecnológica é analisar, por meio do depósito de patentes o desenvolvimento de inovações relacionadas a nanoemulsões frente o Ae. Foram realizadas buscas de patentes nas bases de dados nacionais e internacionais, como o INPI- Instituto Nacional da Propriedade Industrial e EPO- European Patent Office, entre 2015 a 2025, totalizando 12 patentes analisadas. Verificou-se que o Brasil foi o maior depositante, com 9 patentes. As Universidades apresentaram maior percentual como investidores, com 50%. O Código Internacional de Patentes (CIP) da subclasse A01N e o código A61K, foram os mais frequentes. Por fim, com base nesses resultados, observa-se que ainda há um número reduzido de investimentos em patentes destinadas a inovação de nanoemulsões larvicidas, o que demonstra a importância deste estudo para a percepção e incentivo de mais investimentos em inovação tecnológica desta natureza, no Brasil e no mundo.
papers.abstract_zh: 埃及伊蚊是登革热、黄热病、寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅热等主要虫媒病毒的传播媒介。尽管已有多种基于控制蚊虫的策略,但这些方法往往效果不佳,例如蚊虫对化学杀虫剂产生抗性。在此背景下,新的生物技术方法正在被研究,以控制埃及伊蚊。因此,本技术展望旨在通过分析专利池,探讨与针对埃及伊蚊的纳米乳剂相关的创新发展。在2015年至2025年间,对INPI(国家工业产权局)和EPO(欧洲专利局)等国内外数据库进行了专利检索,共分析了12项专利。结果显示,巴西是最大的专利申请国,共申请了9项专利。大学作为投资者的比例最高,达到50%。国际专利分类(CIP)中的子类A01N和A61K是最常见的分类代码。最后,基于这些结果,可以观察到针对杀灭埃及伊蚊的纳米乳剂专利投资仍较为有限,这凸显了本研究的重要性,有助于提高对这类技术创新的认识,并促进巴西及全球范围内的更多投资。
papers.summary_zh: 埃及伊蚊是登革热、黄热病、寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅热等主要虫媒病毒的传播媒介。尽管已有多种基于控制蚊虫的策略,但这些方法往往效果不佳,例如蚊虫对化学杀虫剂产生抗性。在此背景下,新的生物技术方法正在被研究,以控制埃及伊蚊。因此,本技术展望旨在通过分析专利池,探讨与针对埃及伊蚊的纳米乳剂相关的创新发展。在2015年至2025年间,对INPI(国家工业产权局)和EPO(欧洲专利局)等国内外数据库进行了专利检索,共分析了12项专利。结果显示,巴西是最大的专利申请国,共申请了9项专利。大学作为投资者的比例最高,达到50%。国际专利分类(CIP)中的子类A01N和A61K是最常见的分类代码。最后,基于这些结果,可以观察到针对杀灭埃及伊蚊的纳米乳剂专利投资仍较为有限,这凸显了本研究的重要性,有助于提高对这类技术创新的认识,并促进巴西及全球范围内的更多投资。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在了解针对埃及伊蚊的新控制策略的必要性,因为埃及伊蚊是登革热、黄热病、寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅热等主要虫媒病毒的传播媒介。当前策略的无效性,如媒介对化学杀虫剂的抗性,促使了对生物技术创新的探索。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本技术展望分析了2015年至2025年间在INPI和EPO数据库中提交的专利,重点关注与杀灭埃及伊蚊的纳米乳剂相关的创新。共分析了12项专利,其中巴西是最大的专利申请国,提交了9项专利。
analysis_zh.methods: 在2015年至2025年间,对INPI和EPO等国内外数据库进行了专利检索。专利分析基于国际专利分类(CIP)代码,如子类A01N和A61K,以及投资者的识别,包括大学等机构。
analysis_zh.main_results: 结果显示,巴西是最大的专利申请国,共申请了9项专利,大学作为投资者的比例达到50%。在分析的专利中,国际专利分类(CIP)子类A01N和A61K是最常见的分类代码。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,针对杀灭埃及伊蚊的纳米乳剂专利投资仍较为有限,这凸显了本研究的重要性,有助于识别研究空白并推动生物技术领域的创新投资。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 分析专利有助于识别针对埃及伊蚊控制的新创新机会,特别是在基孔肯雅热等依赖有效媒介控制策略的疾病背景下。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅基于专利数据,这限制了对创新有效性和影响的深入分析。证据被认为是中等强度,因为它依赖于专利申请记录,而非实验或临床研究。

news.content_title: Minsap warns about the circulation of chikungunya in Cuba and identifies regions with higher incidence
news.content: Homepage Latest News Cuba News Miami News Blackouts today Informal Exchange Rate Videos Entertainment Sports International News Opinion CiberCuba Interviews United States Cuisine Florida Spain Culture Motor Readings Tourism History Nature Health Close the sidebar ESENFRIT Minsap warns about the circulation of chikungunya in Cuba and identifies areas with higher incidence Latest News By CiberCuba Editorial Team Monday, September 28, 2026 - 6:01 PM Pregnant women should pay special attention to the potential risk of contracting Chikungunya (Reference image)Photo © Periódico 26 The Ministry of Public Health of Cuba (Minsap) confirmed that chikungunya continues to circulate in the country and highlighted Pinar del Río, Sancti Spíritus, Villa Clara, and several municipalities in Havana as areas currently exhibiting the highest incidence rates. «Today we have to say that this disease is circulating in the country. Chikungunya is present», stated the Deputy Minister of Public Health Carilda Peña García during an appearance on Friday in the program Buenos Días, broadcast by Canal Caribe. Peña did not provide an updated national figure of cases during that statement, but explained that the territories with the highest incidence largely coincide with those where fewer people fell ill during the severe epidemic wave last year. "Today we are talking about Pinar del Río, we are talking about Sancti Spíritus, we are talking about Villa Clara, we are talking about a group of territories in Havana," he detailed. According to the epidemiologist, there remains a larger number of people susceptible to illness in those areas because they did not contract the virus during the previous outbreak. news.content_title: Genomic study tracks massive chikungunya epidemic on Réunion Island
news.content: Between August 2024 and June 2025, Réunion Island experienced a massive chikungunya epidemic, with more than 54,000 confirmed cases and 43 deaths, making it the second major Chikungunya virus outbreak on the island after the 2005-2006 epidemic, which had affected about a third of the islands' population. Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne virus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes; while rarely fatal, it causes severe joint pain that can persist for months or years. In 2025, the Réunion epidemic lineage went on to reach other Indian Ocean islands and, over the summer, fuelled unprecedented numbers of cases in more temperate regions of Europe and in China. Throughout the outbreak, the associated Arbovirus National Reference Center in Réunion carried out intensive genomic surveillance, sequencing more than 3,000 near-complete viral genomes across the whole island, a sampling fraction of confirmed cases matched for only a handful of other pathogens, such as Ebola and SARS-CoV-2. This dataset provided a strong basis to track how the virus evolved, spread, and eventually receded. To exploit these data, the team of Belgian, French and American researchers applied phylodynamic and phylogeographic approaches (statistical methods that read the evolutionary relationships between viral genomes to reconstruct where and how a pathogen has travelled). The analyses indicate that the epidemic likely stemmed from a single introduction and that the virus then circulated in a highly intermixed fashion, with frequent movements between municipalities, driven by human mobility and population density. This human-driven spread was especially visible at the peak of the epidemic, with repeated viral exchanges between distant residential areas. The researchers also examined the factors explaining why the epidemic ended. Their models show that the epidemic's dynamics were associated with climatic conditions (temperature and precipitation, which shape mosquito density and activity), but that climate alone cannot account for the decline in transmission. The gradual build-up of population immunity was, in theory, sufficient to push - on its own - the effective reproduction number below 1, bringing the outbreak to an end. With an estimated 66% of the population now immune to the virus, the authors conclude that the risk of a large resurgence is low. This prediction was borne out by the following season, during which only a handful of local cases were reported despite continued chikungunya virus circulation elsewhere in the Indian Ocean. The study shows the value of integrating genomic, demographic, environmental, and immunity data into epidemiological assessment, and points to concrete tools for the future, such as continuous seroprevalence monitoring to anticipate shifts in transmission and targeted vector control. Source: Journal reference: Frumence, E., et al . (2026). Unraveling the epidemiological and dispersal dynamics of the 2024–2025 chikungunya virus epidemic on Réunion Island. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences . DOI: 10.1073/pnas.2621019123. https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2621019123

analysis.brief_en: A genomic study has revealed the dynamics of a massive chikungunya epidemic on Réunion Island between August 2024 and June 2025, which saw over 54,000 confirmed cases and 43 deaths. The virus spread to other Indian Ocean islands and even reached temperate regions of Europe and China. Researchers from Belgium, France, and the United States used phylodynamic and phylogeographic methods to analyze the outbreak, indicating that it likely originated from a single introduction and spread through frequent human movements. The epidemic's decline was attributed to climatic conditions and the gradual build-up of population immunity, with an estimated 66% of the population now immune. This immunity, in theory, was sufficient to bring the effective reproduction number below 1, ending the outbreak. The study highlights the importance of integrating genomic, demographic, environmental, and immunity data for better epidemiological assessment and future preparedness.

news.content_zh: 一项基因组研究揭示了2024年8月至2025年6月期间留尼汪岛大规模基孔肯雅热疫情的动态,该疫情导致超过54,000例确诊病例和43例死亡。该病毒传播到了其他印度洋岛屿,甚至蔓延至欧洲和中国的温带地区。来自比利时、法国和美国的研究人员利用谱系动力学和系统发育地理学方法分析了暴发,表明该疫情可能源于单一引入,并通过频繁的人类活动传播。疫情的下降归因于气候条件和人口免疫力的逐步积累,估计目前有66%的人口已具备免疫力。理论上,这种免疫力足以使有效繁殖数降至1以下,从而结束暴发。该研究强调了整合基因组、人口统计、环境和免疫力数据对于更准确的流行病学评估和未来应对措施的重要性。

news.content: Advanced Search Home News Releases Multimedia Meetings Login Register Illustration 2: analysis of the factors having impacted the course of the massive 2024-2025 chikungunya virus epidemic on Réunion island. (IMAGE) Université libre de Bruxelles Facebook X LinkedIn WeChat Bluesky Message WhatsApp Email Caption The illustration displays four graphics: (A) the cumulative sampling map of the >3,000 viral genomes sequenced to analyse the epidemic; as well as the evolution during the epidemic of (B) the number of confirmed cases in relation to the evolution of climatic variables, (C) the viral population size, and (D) the effective reproduction number (the average number of new infections caused by one infected person at a specific point in time). The analyses show that the epidemic's dynamics were associated with climatic conditions (temperature and precipitation), and that the gradual build-up of population immunity was in theory sufficient to push the effective reproduction number below one, bringing the outbreak to an end. analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study is a partial analysis based on the data provided, and it does not mention any specific investigation, testing, or containment measures. news.title_zh: 图示2:分析影响2024-2025年基孔肯雅病毒疫情在留尼汪岛发展进程的因素 - eurekalert.org
news.source_body_en: This analysis explores the factors influencing the 2024-2025 chikungunya virus epidemic on Réunion island. The study, conducted by the Université libre de Bruxelles, examines the relationship between climatic conditions and the spread of the virus. It highlights the cumulative sampling map of over 3,000 viral genomes and the evolution of confirmed cases in relation to temperature, precipitation, viral population size, and the effective reproduction number. The findings suggest that population immunity could theoretically bring the effective reproduction number below one, ending the outbreak. However, no specific case or death counts are reported. The study is a partial analysis and does not provide details on investigation, testing, or containment measures. The publication date is 2026-09-26, and the event is described as occurring during the 2024-2025 epidemic period. The analysis is based on genomic and epidemiological data, with no indication of unresolved information or hard exclusions.
news.content_zh: 本分析探讨了影响2024-2025年基孔肯雅病毒疫情在留尼汪岛发展的因素。该研究由布鲁塞尔自由大学开展,考察了气候条件与病毒传播之间的关系。它突出了超过3,000例病毒基因组的累积采样地图,以及确认病例的进化与温度、降水量、病毒种群规模和有效繁殖数之间的关系。研究结果表明,群体免疫的逐步积累理论上可以使有效繁殖数降至1以下,从而结束暴发疫情。然而,文中并未报告具体病例或死亡人数。该研究是一项部分分析,未提供关于调查、检测或控制措施的详细信息。发表日期为2026-09-26,事件被描述为发生在2024-2025年疫情期间。该分析基于基因组和流行病学数据,且没有提及未解决的信息或硬性排除情况。

news.wechat_summary_zh: 时间：该研究分析了2024-2025年基孔肯雅病毒疫情在留尼汪岛的发展因素，发表日期为2026-09-26。事件日期未在证据中明确说明...；地点与对象：该分析聚焦于留尼汪岛，该岛是印度洋中的法国海外领地。受影响的人群包括在疫情期间接触过基孔肯雅病毒病毒的个体。；事件：该研究呈现了对2024-2025年基孔肯雅病毒疫情在留尼汪岛发展进程的影响因素的分析。该分析由布鲁塞尔自由大学报道，基于超过3，000例病毒基因组的累积采样地图，以及确认病例的进化与气候变量、病毒种群规模和有效繁殖数之间的关系。；影响与风险：分析表明，疫情的动态与气候条件如温度和降水量相关。研究指出，群体免疫的逐步积累理论上可以降低有效繁殖数至1以下，从而结束暴发疫情。然而，文中未提供具体的病例、死亡或暴露人数数据。；应对与不确定性：该研究是基于现有数据的部分分析，未提及任何具体的调查、检测或控制措施。研究结果是理论性的，基于基因组和流行病学数据，且未提及当前状况或未解决的信息。

news.content: Skip to Content Javascript must be enabled for the correct page display CHP Warns Public About Dengue and Chikungunya Risks During Mid-Autumn Festival Celebrations News China Business TECH ENT Sport HK HotTV Asia Pacific Blog HK News China Business TECH ENT Sport HK HotTV Asia Pacific Blog Font Size A A Home HotNews NEWS CHINA BUSINESS TECH ENT SPORT HK ASIA PACIFIC BLOG HK HK CHP Warns Public About Dengue and Chikungunya Risks During Mid-Autumn Festival Celebrations 2026-09-25 17:15 Last Updated At:09-26 16:12 Facebook Weibo Update on mosquito-borne diseases, dengue fever and chikungunya fever The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health today (September 25) announced the latest situation regarding dengue fever (DF) and chikungunya fever (CF). The CHP also reminded members of the public to take appropriate measures to prevent mosquito bites when engaging in outdoor activities during the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, such as visiting parks, grassy areas and beaches, in order to prevent mosquito-borne diseases. Dengue fever ---------------- From September 18 to yesterday (September 24), the CHP recorded one imported DF case. The patient had visited Malaysia during the incubation period. Hong Kong has recorded 32 DF cases so far this year, comprising 30 imported cases and two local cases. A total of 59 DF cases were recorded last year (2025), all of which were imported cases. In 2024, 161 DF cases were recorded, comprising 156 imported cases and five local cases. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), the global incidence of DF has markedly increased over the past two decades, posing a substantial public health challenge. In 2024, the WHO recorded over 14 million DF cases, which was a record number. In 2025, over five million cases and over 4 000 DF-related deaths were reported in over 90 countries/territories. From January to August 2026, around 2.2 million cases and over 1 000 DF-related deaths have been recorded globally. DF has been prevalent in many neighbouring tourist destinations all along. So far this year, Sri Lanka and Vietnam each recorded over 90 000 cases; Cambodia, Indonesia and Malaysia each recorded over 70 000 cases; Bangladesh recorded over 60 000 cases; and Singapore recorded over 2 400 cases. Meanwhile, according to the Guangdong Provincial Disease Control and Prevention Administration, as of August 31, 2026, Guangdong Province has recorded 431 cases, of which 150 were recorded in August. Detailed information on the latest DF situation in Hong Kong, as well as neighbouring and overseas countries and areas, has been uploaded to the CHP's website. Chikungunya fever ----------------------- From September 18 to yesterday, no new cases of CF had been recorded. Hong Kong has recorded three confirmed CF cases so far this year, including two imported cases and one local case. Hong Kong recorded a total of 82 confirmed CF cases last year. Among them, 11 were local cases and the rest were imported cases. Regarding a local case announced last week (involving a woman living in Tai Kok Tsui), as of 5pm today, the CHP has conducted assessments for over 3 200 individuals residing or working in the district through the health consultation booth, its enquiry hotline, questionnaire surveys and door-to-door visits. No new cases have been identified. Three individuals with mild symptoms previously have been arranged to undergo blood tests and their samples tested negative for the chikungunya virus.The CHP continued to urge members of the public who reside in or have visited the vicinity of Li Tak Street, Cherry Street Park and Lok Kwan Street Park in Tai Kok Tsui to maintain good environmental hygiene and preventive measures. They should seek medical advice and contact the CHP hotline (Tel: 2125 2373)promptly if they have developed a fever, rash or joint pain. According to the WHO, a total of 502 264 CF cases and 186 CF-related deaths were reported in 41 countries/territories last year. Cases were reported in the Americas, Africa, Asia and Europe. According to the Guangdong Provincial Disease Control and Prevention Administration, as of August 31, 2026, Guangdong Province has recorded 739 cases, with 496 recorded in August, a sharp increase from the 36 and 171 cases recorded in June and July respectively. Preventive measures to be taken by the public ---------------------------------------------------- The CHP reminds members of the public to maintain good environmental hygiene, and to take appropriate measures to prevent mosquito bites and mosquito breeding, both in Hong Kong and when travelling to areas affected by mosquito-borne diseases, in order to prevent mosquito-borne diseases. Mosquito-borne diseases such as DF and CF are endemic in various countries worldwide. The risk of importation persists. Members of the public should check the situation at their destinations before travelling abroad, especially when travelling to Southeast Asian countries. Additionally, whether travelling or not, members of the public should use DEET-containing insect repellents or other effective active ingredients properly to prevent mosquito bites, but the following precautions should be taken when using them: read the label instructions carefully first; apply right before entering an area with a risk of mosquito bites; apply on exposed skin and clothing; use DEET of up to 30 per cent for pregnant women and up to 10 per cent for children (for children who travel to countries or areas where mosquito-borne diseases are endemic or epidemic, and where exposure is likely, those aged 2 months or above can use DEET-containing insect repellents with a DEET concentration of up to 30 per cent); apply sunscreen first, then insect repellent; reapply only when needed and follow the instructions; and in addition to DEET, there are other insect repellents available on the market containing different active ingredients, such as IR3535 and picaridin. When using any insect repellent, the public should follow the usage instructions and precautions on the product label. The Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) appeals to members of the public to continue to stay alert and work together to carry out mosquito prevention and control measures early, including inspecting their homes and surroundings to remove potential breeding grounds, changing water in vases and scrubbing their inner surfaces, removing water in saucers under potted plants at least once a week, and properly disposing of containers such as empty cans and lunch boxes. The FEHD also advises members of the public and property management agencies to keep drains free of blockage and level all defective ground surfaces to prevent the accumulation of water. They should also scrub all drains and surface sewers with an alkaline detergent at least once a week to remove any mosquito eggs. The public should call 1823 in case of mosquito problems, and may visit the following pages for more information: the CF page of the CHPand the Travel Health Service, the latest Travel Health News, tips for using insect repellents, and the CHP Facebook Page, Instagram Account and YouTube Channel, and also the Mosquito Prevention and Control dedicated page of the FEHD. The Centre for Health Protection, Photo source: reference image Next Article Public Urged to Take Precautions Against Heat-Related Illnesses During Hot Weather DH reminds public to take precautions against heat-related illnesses during very hot weather The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health (DH) today (September 29) reminded members of the public to take appropriate precautions against heat-related illnesses, such as heat cramps, heat exhaustion and heat stroke, during very hot weather. In a high-temperature environment, excessive sweating and difficulty in heat dissipation can cause stress to the body. Members of the public should take the following precautions: Hydrate in a timely manner to prevent dehydration; Wear light-coloured, loose-fitting and breathable clothing to minimise heat absorption and facilitate perspiration and heat dissipation; Keep indoor areas well ventilated and maintain appropriate temperature and humidity, e.g. by opening windows or using a fan or air-conditioning; Avoid strenuous exercise and prolonged activities such as hiking or trekking; Arrange outdoor activities in the morning or the late afternoon, if possible, and bring enough water; and Avoid beverages containing caffeine, such as coffee and tea, as well as alcoholic beverages, which may speed up water loss through the urinary system. In addition, infants and children, the elderly, pregnant women, individuals with chronic illnesses such as heart disease or high blood pressure, overweight people and outdoor/manual workers are more susceptible to heat stroke. These groups should pay special attention to the following: Infants and young children: Avoid going outside when the temperature is high. If they must go outside, adults should ensure they stay in places with moderate temperatures and good ventilation or air-conditioning. Infants and young children should never be left unattended in a confined space such as a vehicle; The elderly, pregnant women, individuals with chronic illnesses and overweight people: Pay close attention to health conditions and seek help as soon as possible if experiencing any abnormalities in health indicators such as blood pressure, heart rate, etc or if there are fluctuations in health conditions. Avoid going out when the temperature is high. Make sure there is good ventilation, or turn on a fan or air-conditioner to keep an appropriate temperature indoors. High temperatures can also worsen the condition of people with chronic illnesses (such as cardiovascular and respiratory diseases). Therefore, they should have an ample supply of their usual medication and keep in contact with family members, neighbours and the community. People should seek immediate help if they feel unwell. Outdoor/manual workers: Reschedule work to cooler hours as far as feasible. If working in a hot environment is unavoidable, provide shade where practicable and use ventilation and heat dissipation equipment. Once work has begun, gradually adjust the pace of work and take breaks in the shade to regain strength. The DH reminded the public that heat stroke is one of the most common health risks in hot weather. Over the past five years, there have been over 200 hospital admissions due to heat stroke each year in Hong Kong, with two to five fatal cases occurring mainly during the summer months from May to September. Vulnerable groups are more susceptible to heat stroke. Symptoms include dizziness, headache, nausea, shortness of breath or confusion. In severe cases, patients may suffer from convulsions or become unconscious, which can be life-threatening if they are not cooled down and resuscitated in a timely manner. Members of the public are also advised to pay attention to the latest weather, as well as the real-time and forecasted ultraviolet (UV) index released by the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO). When the UV index is high (6 or above), the public should note the following: Avoid direct sunlight exposure to the skin and the eyes; Apply broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen liberally, with a sun protection factor (SPF) of at least 30 or higher, when participating in outdoor activities. Reapply every two hours if staying outdoors for long periods, or after swimming, sweating or towelling off; While using DEET-containing insect repellents for personal protection against mosquito-borne diseases, apply sunscreen before insect repellent; Seek shade; Wear UV-blocking sunglasses; Wear loose-fitting clothing with long-sleeves; and Wear a wide-brimmed hat or use an umbrella. If symptoms develop, such as dizziness, headache, nausea, shortness of breath or confusion, rest and seek help immediately, and seek medical advice as soon as possible. For more health information, the public may visit theCHP's heat strokepage andUV radiation page; the HKO's Dial-a-Weather (1878 200),latestweather report and forecast,UV Indexand weather information forhiking and mountaineering; andpress releasesof the Labour Departmenton precautions against heat stroke for outdoor workers and their employers when the Heat Stress at Work Warning is in force. news.content_original: Skip to Content Javascript must be enabled for the correct page display CHP Warns Public About Dengue and Chikungunya Risks During Mid-Autumn Festival Celebrations News China Business TECH ENT Sport HK HotTV Asia Pacific Blog HK News China Business TECH ENT Sport HK HotTV Asia Pacific Blog Font Size A A Home HotNews NEWS CHINA BUSINESS TECH ENT SPORT HK ASIA PACIFIC BLOG HK HK CHP Warns Public About Dengue and Chikungunya Risks During Mid-Autumn Festival Celebrations 2026-09-25 17:15 Last Updated At:09-26 16:12 Facebook Weibo Update on mosquito-borne diseases, dengue fever and chikungunya fever The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health today (September 25) announced the latest situation regarding dengue fever (DF) and chikungunya fever (CF). The CHP also reminded members of the public to take appropriate measures to prevent mosquito bites when engaging in outdoor activities during the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, such as visiting parks, grassy areas and beaches, in order to prevent mosquito-borne diseases. Dengue fever ---------------- From September 18 to yesterday (September 24), the CHP recorded one imported DF case. The patient had visited Malaysia during the incubation period. Hong Kong has recorded 32 DF cases so far this year, comprising 30 imported cases and two local cases. A total of 59 DF cases were recorded last year (2025), all of which were imported cases. In 2024, 161 DF cases were recorded, comprising 156 imported cases and five local cases. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), the global incidence of DF has markedly increased over the past two decades, posing a substantial public health challenge. In 2024, the WHO recorded over 14 million DF cases, which was a record number. In 2025, over five million cases and over 4 000 DF-related deaths were reported in over 90 countries/territories. From January to August 2026, around 2.2 million cases and over 1 000 DF-related deaths have been recorded globally. DF has been prevalent in many neighbouring tourist destinations all along. So far this year, Sri Lanka and Vietnam each recorded over 90 000 cases; Cambodia, Indonesia and Malaysia each recorded over 70 000 cases; Bangladesh recorded over 60 000 cases; and Singapore recorded over 2 400 cases. Meanwhile, according to the Guangdong Provincial Disease Control and Prevention Administration, as of August 31, 2026, Guangdong Province has recorded 431 cases, of which 150 were recorded in August. Detailed information on the latest DF situation in Hong Kong, as well as neighbouring and overseas countries and areas, has been uploaded to the CHP's website. Chikungunya fever ----------------------- From September 18 to yesterday, no new cases of CF had been recorded. Hong Kong has recorded three confirmed CF cases so far this year, including two imported cases and one local case. Hong Kong recorded a total of 82 confirmed CF cases last year. Among them, 11 were local cases and the rest were imported cases. Regarding a local case announced last week (involving a woman living in Tai Kok Tsui), as of 5pm today, the CHP has conducted assessments for over 3 200 individuals residing or working in the district through the health consultation booth, its enquiry hotline, questionnaire surveys and door-to-door visits. No new cases have been identified. Three individuals with mild symptoms previously have been arranged to undergo blood tests and their samples tested negative for the chikungunya virus.The CHP continued to urge members of the public who reside in or have visited the vicinity of Li Tak Street, Cherry Street Park and Lok Kwan Street Park in Tai Kok Tsui to maintain good environmental hygiene and preventive measures. They should seek medical advice and contact the CHP hotline (Tel: 2125 2373)promptly if they have developed a fever, rash or joint pain. According to the WHO, a total of 502 264 CF cases and 186 CF-related deaths were reported in 41 countries/territories last year. Cases were reported in the Americas, Africa, Asia and Europe. According to the Guangdong Provincial Disease Control and Prevention Administration, as of August 31, 2026, Guangdong Province has recorded 739 cases, with 496 recorded in August, a sharp increase from the 36 and 171 cases recorded in June and July respectively. Preventive measures to be taken by the public ---------------------------------------------------- The CHP reminds members of the public to maintain good environmental hygiene, and to take appropriate measures to prevent mosquito bites and mosquito breeding, both in Hong Kong and when travelling to areas affected by mosquito-borne diseases, in order to prevent mosquito-borne diseases. Mosquito-borne diseases such as DF and CF are endemic in various countries worldwide. The risk of importation persists. Members of the public should check the situation at their destinations before travelling abroad, especially when travelling to Southeast Asian countries. Additionally, whether travelling or not, members of the public should use DEET-containing insect repellents or other effective active ingredients properly to prevent mosquito bites, but the following precautions should be taken when using them: read the label instructions carefully first; apply right before entering an area with a risk of mosquito bites; apply on exposed skin and clothing; use DEET of up to 30 per cent for pregnant women and up to 10 per cent for children (for children who travel to countries or areas where mosquito-borne diseases are endemic or epidemic, and where exposure is likely, those aged 2 months or above can use DEET-containing insect repellents with a DEET concentration of up to 30 per cent); apply sunscreen first, then insect repellent; reapply only when needed and follow the instructions; and in addition to DEET, there are other insect repellents available on the market containing different active ingredients, such as IR3535 and picaridin. When using any insect repellent, the public should follow the usage instructions and precautions on the product label. The Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) appeals to members of the public to continue to stay alert and work together to carry out mosquito prevention and control measures early, including inspecting their homes and surroundings to remove potential breeding grounds, changing water in vases and scrubbing their inner surfaces, removing water in saucers under potted plants at least once a week, and properly disposing of containers such as empty cans and lunch boxes. The FEHD also advises members of the public and property management agencies to keep drains free of blockage and level all defective ground surfaces to prevent the accumulation of water. They should also scrub all drains and surface sewers with an alkaline detergent at least once a week to remove any mosquito eggs. The public should call 1823 in case of mosquito problems, and may visit the following pages for more information: the CF page of the CHPand the Travel Health Service, the latest Travel Health News, tips for using insect repellents, and the CHP Facebook Page, Instagram Account and YouTube Channel, and also the Mosquito Prevention and Control dedicated page of the FEHD. The Centre for Health Protection, Photo source: reference image Next Article Public Urged to Take Precautions Against Heat-Related Illnesses During Hot Weather DH reminds public to take precautions against heat-related illnesses during very hot weather The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health (DH) today (September 29) reminded members of the public to take appropriate precautions against heat-related illnesses, such as heat cramps, heat exhaustion and heat stroke, during very hot weather. In a high-temperature environment, excessive sweating and difficulty in heat dissipation can cause stress to the body. Members of the public should take the following precautions: Hydrate in a timely manner to prevent dehydration; Wear light-coloured, loose-fitting and breathable clothing to minimise heat absorption and facilitate perspiration and heat dissipation; Keep indoor areas well ventilated and maintain appropriate temperature and humidity, e.g. by opening windows or using a fan or air-conditioning; Avoid strenuous exercise and prolonged activities such as hiking or trekking; Arrange outdoor activities in the morning or the late afternoon, if possible, and bring enough water; and Avoid beverages containing caffeine, such as coffee and tea, as well as alcoholic beverages, which may speed up water loss through the urinary system. In addition, infants and children, the elderly, pregnant women, individuals with chronic illnesses such as heart disease or high blood pressure, overweight people and outdoor/manual workers are more susceptible to heat stroke. These groups should pay special attention to the following: Infants and young children: Avoid going outside when the temperature is high. If they must go outside, adults should ensure they stay in places with moderate temperatures and good ventilation or air-conditioning. Infants and young children should never be left unattended in a confined space such as a vehicle; The elderly, pregnant women, individuals with chronic illnesses and overweight people: Pay close attention to health conditions and seek help as soon as possible if experiencing any abnormalities in health indicators such as blood pressure, heart rate, etc or if there are fluctuations in health conditions. Avoid going out when the temperature is high. Make sure there is good ventilation, or turn on a fan or air-conditioner to keep an appropriate temperature indoors. High temperatures can also worsen the condition of people with chronic illnesses (such as cardiovascular and respiratory diseases). Therefore, they should have an ample supply of their usual medication and keep in contact with family members, neighbours and the community. People should seek immediate help if they feel unwell. Outdoor/manual workers: Reschedule work to cooler hours as far as feasible. If working in a hot environment is unavoidable, provide shade where practicable and use ventilation and heat dissipation equipment. Once work has begun, gradually adjust the pace of work and take breaks in the shade to regain strength. The DH reminded the public that heat stroke is one of the most common health risks in hot weather. Over the past five years, there have been over 200 hospital admissions due to heat stroke each year in Hong Kong, with two to five fatal cases occurring mainly during the summer months from May to September. Vulnerable groups are more susceptible to heat stroke. Symptoms include dizziness, headache, nausea, shortness of breath or confusion. In severe cases, patients may suffer from convulsions or become unconscious, which can be life-threatening if they are not cooled down and resuscitated in a timely manner. Members of the public are also advised to pay attention to the latest weather, as well as the real-time and forecasted ultraviolet (UV) index released by the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO). When the UV index is high (6 or above), the public should note the following: Avoid direct sunlight exposure to the skin and the eyes; Apply broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen liberally, with a sun protection factor (SPF) of at least 30 or higher, when participating in outdoor activities. Reapply every two hours if staying outdoors for long periods, or after swimming, sweating or towelling off; While using DEET-containing insect repellents for personal protection against mosquito-borne diseases, apply sunscreen before insect repellent; Seek shade; Wear UV-blocking sunglasses; Wear loose-fitting clothing with long-sleeves; and Wear a wide-brimmed hat or use an umbrella. If symptoms develop, such as dizziness, headache, nausea, shortness of breath or confusion, rest and seek help immediately, and seek medical advice as soon as possible. For more health information, the public may visit theCHP's heat strokepage andUV radiation page; the HKO's Dial-a-Weather (1878 200),latestweather report and forecast,UV Indexand weather information forhiking and mountaineering; andpress releasesof the Labour Departmenton precautions against heat stroke for outdoor workers and their employers when the Heat Stress at Work Warning is in force. news.source_body_en: Between August 2024 and June 2025, Réunion Island experienced a massive chikungunya epidemic, with more than 54,000 confirmed cases and 43 deaths. It was the island's second major chikungunya virus.
news.content_zh: 2024年8月至2025年6月期间,留尼汪岛经历了大规模的基孔肯雅热疫情,报告了超过54,000例确诊病例和43例死亡病例。这是该岛第二次发生严重的基孔肯雅病毒疫情。
news.summary_zh: 2024年8月至2025年6月期间,留尼汪岛经历了大规模的基孔肯雅热疫情,报告了超过54,000例确诊病例和43例死亡病例。这是该岛第二次发生严重的基孔肯雅病毒疫情。

analysis_zh.location_and_population: 这是该岛第二次发生严重的基孔肯雅病毒疫情。
analysis_zh.event: 发生了一次大规模的基孔肯雅热疫情,报告了超过54,000例确诊病例和43例死亡病例。研究指出,该病毒可能曾一次进入该岛并随后通过人类活动传播。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 报告了超过54,000例确诊病例和43例死亡病例。疫情对健康和运营造成了重大影响,但没有明确说明风险等级。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 该研究提出了关于病毒引入和传播的假设,但没有报告具体的调查、检测或控制措施细节。

news.wechat_summary_zh: 时间：2024年8月至2025年6月之间。；地点与对象：这是该岛第二次发生严重的基孔肯雅病毒疫情。；事件：发生了一次大规模的基孔肯雅热疫情，报告了超过54，000例确诊病例和43例死亡病例。研究指出，该病毒可能曾一次进入该岛并随后通过人类活动传播。；影响与风险：报告了超过54，000例确诊病例和43例死亡病例。疫情对健康和运营造成了重大影响，但没有明确说明风险等级。；应对与不确定性：该研究提出了关于病毒引入和传播的假设，但没有报告具体的调查、检测或控制措施细节。

Photo: Kerala Kaumudi. THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: The Health Department issued an alert regarding the spread of diseases such as Dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika, noting the risk of mosquito breeding in stagnant water caused by intermittent rains. Health and Devaswom Minister K Muraleedharan stated that comprehensive preventive measures are essential to curb the spread of these diseases and urged the public to adhere to the department's guidelines. Symptoms of dengue fever include high fever, headache, body aches, rashes, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Seek immediate medical attention at a hospital if symptoms appear; do not attempt self-medication. Doctors advise complete rest and the consumption of plenty of fluids as soon as symptoms are experienced. There is a high likelihood of Aedes mosquitoes breeding and multiplying during the intermittent rains. A 'Dry Day' should be observed by eliminating potential mosquito breeding sites: at educational institutions on Fridays, at workplaces on Saturdays, and in homes on Sundays. Inside the house, care must be taken to prevent water stagnation—and consequent mosquito breeding—in areas such as the tray behind the refrigerator, the saucers under flowerpots, containers holding ornamental plants grown in water, and unused toilet bowls. One should adopt personal protective measures against mosquito bites while engaging in source reduction activities. It is essential to wear light-colored clothing that covers the entire body, apply mosquito repellents, and ensure protection by using a mosquito net while sleeping. THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: The Health Department issued an alert regarding the spread of diseases such as Dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika, noting the risk of mosquito breeding in stagnant water caused by intermittent rains. Health and Devaswom Minister K Muraleedharan stated that comprehensive preventive measures are essential to curb the spread of these diseases and urged the public to adhere to the department's guidelines. Symptoms of dengue fever include high fever, headache, body aches, rashes, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Seek immediate medical attention at a hospital if symptoms appear; do not attempt self-medication. Doctors advise complete rest and the consumption of plenty of fluids as soon as symptoms are experienced. There is a high likelihood of Aedes mosquitoes breeding and multiplying during the intermittent rains. A 'Dry Day' should be observed by eliminating potential mosquito breeding sites: at educational institutions on Fridays, at workplaces on Saturdays, and in homes on Sundays. Inside the house, care must be taken to prevent water stagnation—and consequent mosquito breeding—in areas such as the tray behind the refrigerator, the saucers under flowerpots, containers holding ornamental plants grown in water, and unused toilet bowls. One should adopt personal protective measures against mosquito bites while engaging in source reduction activities. It is essential to wear light-colored clothing that covers the entire body, apply mosquito repellents, and ensure protection by using a mosquito net while sleeping. news.wechat_summary_zh: 时间：卫生部门于2026年9月23日发布了警报，该警告是针对本月早些时候开始的间歇性降雨而发布的。；地点与对象：该警报由喀拉拉邦卫生部门发布，覆盖整个喀拉拉邦，包括Thevara Bridge等地区。受影响的人群包括喀拉拉邦居民，尤其是那些居住在积水区域的居民。；事件：喀拉拉邦卫生部门因间歇性降雨导致积水中的蚊虫繁殖风险而发布了关于登革热、基孔肯雅热和寨卡病毒传播的警告。这是基于官方声明确认的事件。；影响与风险：该警告强调了降雨期间Aedes蚊虫繁殖的高可能性，这可能导致登革热、基孔肯雅热和寨卡病毒的传播。卫生部门强调了采取预防措施以遏制传播的必要性，但证据中未报告具体病例或死亡人数。；应对与不确定性：卫生部门已启动预防措施，包括公众意识宣传活动和‘干日’活动以消除蚊虫繁殖地。响应仍在进行中，基于部门的指南，证据中未提及任何解决迹象或进一步细节。

supplementary_news.content_title: Genomic study tracks massive chikungunya epidemic on Réunion Island
supplementary_news.content: Between August 2024 and June 2025, Réunion Island experienced a massive chikungunya epidemic, with more than 54,000 confirmed cases and 43 deaths, making it the second major Chikungunya virus outbreak on the island after the 2005-2006 epidemic, which had affected about a third of the islands' population. Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne virus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes; while rarely fatal, it causes severe joint pain that can persist for months or years. In 2025, the Réunion epidemic lineage went on to reach other Indian Ocean islands and, over the summer, fuelled unprecedented numbers of cases in more temperate regions of Europe and in China. Throughout the outbreak, the associated Arbovirus National Reference Center in Réunion carried out intensive genomic surveillance, sequencing more than 3,000 near-complete viral genomes across the whole island, a sampling fraction of confirmed cases matched for only a handful of other pathogens, such as Ebola and SARS-CoV-2. This dataset provided a strong basis to track how the virus evolved, spread, and eventually receded. To exploit these data, the team of Belgian, French and American researchers applied phylodynamic and phylogeographic approaches (statistical methods that read the evolutionary relationships between viral genomes to reconstruct where and how a pathogen has travelled). The analyses indicate that the epidemic likely stemmed from a single introduction and that the virus then circulated in a highly intermixed fashion, with frequent movements between municipalities, driven by human mobility and population density. This human-driven spread was especially visible at the peak of the epidemic, with repeated viral exchanges between distant residential areas. The researchers also examined the factors explaining why the epidemic ended. Their models show that the epidemic's dynamics were associated with climatic conditions (temperature and precipitation, which shape mosquito density and activity), but that climate alone cannot account for the decline in transmission. The gradual build-up of population immunity was, in theory, sufficient to push - on its own - the effective reproduction number below 1, bringing the outbreak to an end. With an estimated 66% of the population now immune to the virus, the authors conclude that the risk of a large resurgence is low. This prediction was borne out by the following season, during which only a handful of local cases were reported despite continued chikungunya virus circulation elsewhere in the Indian Ocean. The study shows the value of integrating genomic, demographic, environmental, and immunity data into epidemiological assessment, and points to concrete tools for the future, such as continuous seroprevalence monitoring to anticipate shifts in transmission and targeted vector control. Source: Journal reference: Frumence, E., et al . (2026). Unraveling the epidemiological and dispersal dynamics of the 2024–2025 chikungunya virus epidemic on Réunion Island. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences . DOI: 10.1073/pnas.2621019123. https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2621019123
